title: Odd covering system
statement_plain: A covering system is a finite set of congruences (each of the form 'n ≡ a mod m') with distinct moduli such that every integer satisfies at least one. Is there one in which every modulus is odd?
attack_angle: Search for an odd distinct covering system computationally, e.g. constraint/SAT search over bounded sets of odd moduli.

title: Odd numbers not of the form prime + two powers of 2
statement_plain: Let A be the set of odd integers ≥ 1 that cannot be written as p + 2^k + 2^l with p prime and k,l ≥ 0. Does A have positive upper density?
attack_angle: Sieve integers up to large N, mark those representable as p+2^k+2^l, and estimate the density of the exceptional set.

title: Every large integer as prime plus few powers of 2
statement_plain: Is there some fixed k such that every large integer can be written as a prime plus at most k powers of 2?
attack_angle: For each candidate k, test all integers up to large N and look for integers requiring more than k powers of 2 (counterexample search).

title: Large odd integers as squarefree plus power of 2
statement_plain: Is every large odd integer n the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2?
attack_angle: Counterexample search: for each odd n up to large N, check whether some n - 2^k is squarefree.

title: Primes representing all small even numbers as prime differences
statement_plain: Are there infinitely many primes p such that every even number n ≤ p-3 can be written as a difference of two primes q1 - q2 with both q1,q2 ≤ p?
attack_angle: Enumerate primes p, build the set of achievable prime differences with both primes ≤ p, and check coverage of all even n ≤ p-3.

title: Practical numbers needing few divisors
statement_plain: A number m is 'practical' if every integer 1 ≤ n < m is a sum of distinct divisors of m; let h(m) be the number of divisors that always suffice. Are there infinitely many practical m with h(m) < (log log m)^{O(1)}, and is h(n!) small?
attack_angle: Compute practical numbers and the exact h(m) via subset-sum over divisors, tabulate h(m) and h(n!) to test the conjectured growth.

title: Consecutive primes in arithmetic progression
statement_plain: For each k ≥ 3, are there k consecutive primes that form an arithmetic progression (equally spaced with no primes in between)?
attack_angle: Distributed prime-gap search for runs of k consecutive primes in AP, extending known records for larger k.

title: Counting ways to write 1 as distinct unit fractions
statement_plain: Let F(k) be the number of ways to write 1 = 1/n_1 + ... + 1/n_k with distinct positive integers n_1 < ... < n_k. Find good estimates for F(k).
attack_angle: Exact enumeration of all Egyptian-fraction representations of 1 with k terms for growing k to extend the known sequence and fit growth models.

title: Sidon set sizes grow slowly
statement_plain: Let F(N) be the size of the largest Sidon set in {1,...,N} (a set with all pairwise sums distinct). Is it true that for every k, F(N+k) ≤ F(N)+1 for all large N?
attack_angle: Compute F(N) exactly for small N (maximum-clique / ILP search) and check the increment F(N+k) - F(N) for counterexamples.

title: Small maximal Sidon sets
statement_plain: Does there exist a maximal Sidon set inside {1,...,N} (one that cannot be extended) of size only O(N^{1/3})?
attack_angle: Greedy/backtracking search for maximal (non-extendable) Sidon sets of unusually small size across many N.

title: Longest arithmetic progression of primes
statement_plain: Does the longest arithmetic progression of primes contained in {1,...,N} have length o(log N)?
attack_angle: Compute the longest AP of primes in {1,...,N} for large N and compare its growth against log N.

title: Numbers coprime to 6 with no prime of a special form
statement_plain: Is there an integer m ≥ 1 with gcd(m,6)=1 such that none of the numbers 2^k * 3^l * m + 1 are prime, for any k,l ≥ 0?
attack_angle: Search over m coprime to 6 using covering-congruence reasoning, testing candidate m for primality of 2^k 3^l m + 1 over bounded k,l.

title: Monotonicity statistics of prime gaps
statement_plain: Let d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n be the nth prime gap. Do the n with d_{n+1} ≥ d_n have density 1/2 (and likewise d_{n+1} ≤ d_n), and are there infinitely many n with d_{n+1} = d_n?
attack_angle: Compute prime gaps to large N and empirically track the densities of increasing/decreasing/equal consecutive gaps.

title: Sum of squares of prime gaps
statement_plain: Let d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n. Prove that the sum of d_n^2 for n ≤ N is O(N (log N)^2).
attack_angle: Compute the running sum of squared prime gaps up to large N and compare against N (log N)^2 to build evidence and locate extremal gaps.

title: Representations as prime plus a power of two
statement_plain: Let f(n) count the ways to write n = p + 2^k with p prime and k ≥ 0. Is it true that f(n) = o(log n)?
attack_angle: Compute f(n) up to large N (few powers of 2 per n) and search for n where f(n) grows close to log n.

title: Largest B_3^+ set (distinct triple sums)
statement_plain: Let f(N) be the largest size of a subset A of {1,...,N} in which all triple sums a+b+c are distinct (apart from trivial coincidences). Is f(N) asymptotic to N^{1/3}?
attack_angle: Compute the largest such set for small N by ILP/backtracking and compare exact sizes with N^{1/3}.

title: Gaps in unit-fraction representations of 1
statement_plain: For any distinct integers 1 < n_1 < ... < n_k with 1 = 1/n_1 + ... + 1/n_k, must the largest gap max(n_{i+1} - n_i) be at least 3?
attack_angle: Enumerate Egyptian-fraction representations of 1 and check the maximum consecutive-denominator gap for any counterexample below 3.

title: Numerator of the harmonic sum vs lcm
statement_plain: Write the harmonic sum 1 + 1/2 + ... + 1/n as a_n / L_n where L_n = lcm(1,...,n). Do both gcd(a_n,L_n) = 1 and gcd(a_n,L_n) > 1 occur for infinitely many n?
attack_angle: Compute a_n and gcd(a_n, L_n) for large n and record how often the gcd exceeds 1.

title: Smallest denominator never used in a k-term unit-fraction sum of 1
statement_plain: For each k, let v(k) be the smallest positive integer that never appears as one of the denominators n_i in any representation 1 = 1/n_1 + ... + 1/n_k with distinct n_i. Estimate how v(k) grows.
attack_angle: Enumerate k-term Egyptian-fraction representations of 1, record which denominators are achievable, and compute v(k) for small k.

title: Egyptian fractions with large denominators
statement_plain: Let k(N) be the fewest terms needed to write 1 = 1/n_1 + ... + 1/n_k using distinct integers all at least N. Does k(N) - (e-1)N tend to infinity?
attack_angle: Compute k(N) exactly for small N via constructive/optimal search and compare against (e-1)N.

title: Largest set avoiding a unit-fraction identity
statement_plain: Let f(N) be the largest subset A of {1,...,N} with no solution to 1/a = 1/b_1 + ... + 1/b_k using distinct elements of A. Estimate f(N); is it (1/2 + o(1))N?
attack_angle: Find the largest such set for small N by ILP / constraint search and compare its size against N/2.

title: Largest set avoiding 1/a = 1/b + 1/c
statement_plain: Let f(N) be the largest subset A of {1,...,N} with no three distinct elements satisfying 1/a = 1/b + 1/c. Estimate f(N); is it (1/2 + o(1))N?
attack_angle: Model as a maximum independent set on the hypergraph of forbidden triples and compute exact f(N) for small N.

title: Length of Egyptian-fraction expansions
statement_plain: For 1 ≤ a < b let N(a,b) be the fewest unit fractions with distinct denominators > 1 summing to a/b, and set N(b) = max over a of N(a,b). Is N(b) = O(log log b)?
attack_angle: Compute N(a,b) for all a < b up to moderate b (dynamic programming / greedy plus refinement) and track the maximum against log log b.

title: Product of two reciprocal prime sums equal to 1
statement_plain: Are there two finite sets of primes P and Q such that (sum of 1/p over P) times (sum of 1/q over Q) equals exactly 1?
attack_angle: Search over finite prime sets, computing reciprocal sums as exact rationals and testing whether two products multiply to 1.

title: Closest a subset sum of unit fractions gets to 1
statement_plain: Let delta(N) be the smallest nonzero value of |1 - sum of 1/n over A| as A ranges over subsets of {1,...,N}. Is delta(N) = exp(-(c+o(1))N) for some constant c in (0,1)?
attack_angle: Compute delta(N) exactly for small N by subset-sum over rationals and fit the exponential decay constant.

title: Sums of prime reciprocals equal to 1 - 1/m
statement_plain: Are there infinitely many solutions to 1/p_1 + ... + 1/p_k = 1 - 1/m with m ≥ 2 an integer and p_1 < ... < p_k distinct primes?
attack_angle: Search over sets of distinct primes, computing reciprocal sums exactly and checking whether the complement to 1 is a unit fraction.

title: Sums of k many kth powers
statement_plain: For k ≥ 3, let A be the kth powers and count the representations of n as a sum of k many kth powers. Is there some c > 0 and infinitely many n with more than n^c representations?
attack_angle: Enumerate representations of n as sums of k kth powers up to large N and look for n with unusually many representations.

title: Polynomial with all pairwise sums distinct
statement_plain: Does there exist an integer polynomial f(x) such that all the sums f(a) + f(b) with a < b nonnegative integers are distinct (making {f(n)} a Sidon set)?
attack_angle: Test candidate polynomials by computing f(a)+f(b) over a bounded range and searching for collisions.

title: Growth of the greedy Sidon sequence
statement_plain: Build a set greedily: start with 1 and repeatedly add the smallest integer that keeps the set Sidon (all pairwise sums distinct), giving 1,2,4,8,13,21,31,45,66,81,97,.... How fast does this sequence grow?
attack_angle: Extend the greedy Sidon sequence far and empirically fit its counting-function growth against N^{1/2}.

title: Distinct prime divisors covering a run of composites
statement_plain: If n+1, ..., n+k are all composite, must there always exist distinct primes p_1, ..., p_k with p_i dividing n+i for each i (a system of distinct representatives)?
attack_angle: For each maximal run of composites, build the bipartite divisibility graph and test for a perfect matching (Hall's condition) as a counterexample check.

title: Symmetric sums of nearby primes
statement_plain: Let f(n) be the minimum over i<n of p_{n+i} + p_{n-i}, where p_k is the kth prime. Is limsup (f(n) - 2 p_n) infinite?
attack_angle: Compute f(n) - 2 p_n over large ranges of n and search for increasingly large values.

title: An inequality between lcm's at consecutive primes
statement_plain: Let [1,...,n] denote lcm(1,...,n). Is it true that for all k, [1,...,p_{k+1}-1] < p_k * [1,...,p_k], where p_k is the kth prime?
attack_angle: Directly verify the lcm inequality for all k up to large bounds using exact big-integer arithmetic.

title: Odd weird numbers and primitive weird numbers
statement_plain: A number n is 'weird' if the sum of its proper divisors exceeds n yet no subset of its divisors sums to n. Are there any odd weird numbers, and are there infinitely many primitive weird numbers (none of whose proper divisors are weird)?
attack_angle: Distributed search testing candidates for weirdness via subset-sum over divisors, focused on odd n and on generating primitive weird numbers.

title: Largest Sidon set among the squares
statement_plain: What is the size of the largest Sidon set contained in {1, 2^2, 3^2, ..., N^2} (a subset of the squares with all pairwise sums distinct)? Is it N^{1-o(1)}?
attack_angle: Compute maximum Sidon subsets of the first N squares for growing N and compare sizes against N^{1-o(1)}.

title: Primorial plus a prime being prime
statement_plain: Let P be the product of the first n primes. Does there always exist a prime p between p_n and P such that P + p is also prime?
attack_angle: For each n, compute the primorial P and test P + p for primality over primes p in (p_n, P) until one is found (or a counterexample emerges).

title: Three consecutive shared prime-factor sets
statement_plain: Can there exist two distinct integers x and y such that x and y have the same set of prime factors, x+1 and y+1 have the same set of prime factors, and x+2 and y+2 also have the same set of prime factors?
attack_angle: Compute the radical (set of prime factors) of consecutive integers and search for two positions x,y whose three consecutive radicals all match.

title: Runs of distinct prime gaps
statement_plain: Let d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n. Let h(x) be the longest run of consecutive gaps d_n, d_{n+1}, ..., all distinct, starting at some n < x. Estimate h(x); is it larger than (log x)^c and also o(log x)?
attack_angle: Scan prime gaps up to large x and compute the longest run of pairwise-distinct consecutive gaps.

title: Smallest even number that is not yet a prime gap
statement_plain: Let d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n. Let r(x) be the smallest even integer t that does not occur as any gap d_n for n ≤ x. Does r(x) tend to infinity (or even r(x)/log x)?
attack_angle: Compute the set of prime gaps up to x and find the smallest missing even value r(x) for growing x.

title: Subadditivity of the prime-counting function
statement_plain: If pi(x) counts primes up to x, is it true that pi(x+y) ≤ pi(x) + pi(y) for all large x and y?
attack_angle: Counterexample search: compute pi over ranges and test pi(x+y) ≤ pi(x) + pi(y), targeting prime-rich short intervals.

title: Few divisors in a short interval near the square root
statement_plain: For fixed epsilon > 0, is it true that for all large n the number of divisors of n lying in the interval (sqrt(n), sqrt(n) + n^{1/2 - epsilon}) is bounded (O_epsilon(1))?
attack_angle: Factor integers up to large N and count divisors falling just above sqrt(n) to look for n with many such divisors.

title: Consecutive integers with distinct divisor counts
statement_plain: Let F(x) be the longest run of consecutive integers n+1, ..., n+k up to x whose divisor counts tau(n+i) are all distinct. Estimate F(x); is F(x) ≤ (log x)^{O(1)}?
attack_angle: Compute the divisor function over long ranges and find the longest run of consecutive integers with pairwise-distinct tau values.

title: Integers as a sum of the smallest divisors of some m
statement_plain: Let f(n) be the smallest m such that n equals the sum of the k smallest divisors of m for some k ≥ 1. Is f(n) = o(n) (at least for almost all n)?
attack_angle: For each n search increasing m, summing smallest divisors of m to hit n, and tabulate f(n) against n.

title: Primes p with p - k! always composite
statement_plain: Are there infinitely many primes p such that p - k! is composite for every k with 1 ≤ k! < p?
attack_angle: Sieve primes and test each against subtraction of all factorials below it, collecting those where every p - k! is composite.

title: Sierpinski numbers without a finite covering set
statement_plain: A Sierpinski number is an odd m such that none of 2^k m + 1 are prime. A finite covering set is a finite set of primes such that every 2^k m + 1 is divisible by one of them. Are there Sierpinski numbers with no finite covering set of primes?
attack_angle: Study candidate Sierpinski numbers computationally, checking whether their sequences 2^k m + 1 admit a finite covering set of prime divisors.

title: Integers with n - 2^k always prime
statement_plain: Are there infinitely many n (or any n > 105) such that n - 2^k is prime for every power of two 2^k with 1 < 2^k < n?
attack_angle: Counterexample/existence search: for each n test primality of all n - 2^k with 2^k < n, looking for any n > 105 that works.

title: Sidon sets among the cubes
statement_plain: Does {1, 2^3, ..., N^3} contain a Sidon set of size proportional to N? Is there an infinite set A of positive density such that the cubes {a^3 : a in A} form a Sidon set?
attack_angle: Search for large Sidon subsets of the first N cubes and estimate their maximal size as a fraction of N.
